gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Tesla rates the Model Y 12V socket at 12 A continuous (16 A peak) while UGREEN labels its 145 W retractable charger for 17.8 A input and Anker's 167.5 W charger needs at least 14 A at 12 V just to make its rated output, so only the Anker 535 (7.2 A input) fits a Tesla or a 10 A-fused socket at full rating.
standout_why: Compared against soldermag.com and supergrail.com (both opened): supergrail gives 12–24 V input for the Anker 535 and UGREEN 130 W, a generic '10 A fuse' example and the 5 A e-marked cable rule; soldermag gives the 45+9+9 W three-port split. Neither names a vehicle socket rating or any charger's rated input amps. The two cited WIRED pages could not be opened (wired.com and archive blocked); ChatGPT's paraphrase of WIRED says only 'provided your car socket supports the load' with no number. thisusb.com and dashanddrive.com failed on TLS and were not read.
decides: It overturns the 'best high power' pick for EV and small-car owners: a Tesla's 12 A socket can supply roughly 150 W input, so the 145 W UGREEN (17.8 A label) and 167.5 W Anker (≥14 A by arithmetic) cannot hit their ratings there, and Anker's own test by techtest.org shows the A2737 cycles off rather than throttling. The Anker 535 at 7.2 A is the only candidate whose maker-rated draw fits every 10 A socket, but Anker US lists it sold out today, so the realistic 'fits-any-socket' pick becomes the Anker 75 W retractable (45 W cable + 30 W port). It also confirms a protocol limit: the Anker 75 W's PPS stops at 11 V 3 A, so Samsung 45 W Super Fast Charging 2.0 only runs on UGREEN's C2 port (PPS 5–21 V 5 A).

findings.label: 12V socket rating
findings.source_title: Tesla Model Y Owner's Manual – Interior Electronics (low voltage power outlet)
findings.note: Tesla's own manual mirror; exact text 'suitable for accessories requiring up to 12A continuous draw (16A peak)'. Power only when vehicle in use or a user is detected unless 'Keep Accessory Power On' is enabled. Tesla recommends against non-Tesla accessories. At a nominal 12.5 V, 12 A ≈ 150 W input.

findings.label: rated input
findings.source_title: ChargerLAB – Teardown of UGREEN Nexode Car Charger 145W with Retractable USB-C Cable (EC604)
findings.note: Read from UGREEN's product label photographed by ChargerLAB. 17.8 A exceeds Tesla's 12 A continuous and any 10 A or 15 A accessory fuse. UGREEN US page returned HTTP 429 three times.

findings.label: per-port PDO and PPS
findings.value: C2: 20 V 5 A (100 W), PPS 5–21 V 5 A; retractable cable: 20 V 3 A (60 W), PPS 5–11 V 3 A; C1: 12 V 2.5 A (30 W), PPS 5–11 V 3 A; USB-A: 12 V 2.5 A
findings.source_title: ChargerLAB – Teardown of UGREEN Nexode EC604
findings.note: Measured with KM003C at 12 V input; ChargerLAB reports identical PDOs at simulated 24 V input. Only C2 can satisfy Samsung 45 W Super Fast Charging 2.0 (needs PPS ≥20 V 2.25 A). Protocols: PD3.0, PPS, QC3.0/4+/5, SCP, FCP, AFC.

findings.label: output limits
findings.value: cable: 20 V 2.25 A (45 W), PPS 5–11 V 3 A (30 W); port: 15 V 2 A (30 W), PPS 5–11 V 3 A
findings.source_title: Anker Support – Anker Nano Car Charger (75W, USB-C Port, Built-In Retractable USB-C Cable) specifications
findings.note: PPS tops out at 11 V 3 A on both outputs, so Samsung's 45 W PPS tier is not reachable; 45 W over fixed 20 V PD works for MacBook Air-class laptops. Anker's page does not state input current or the two-device split.

findings.label: rated input and port split
findings.value: 12–24 V DC, 7.2 A; 3 ports: C1 45 W via PD/PPS; C2 + USB-A together: 9 W each; single USB-C: 20 V 3.35 A (67 W)
findings.note: 7.2 A is the only candidate input rating under Tesla's 12 A continuous and a 10 A fuse. Anker US shows 'Sold out / Notify Me' today, no base price displayed. Includes 3.2 ft USB-C to USB-C cable (rating not stated).

findings.label: minimum input current at 12 V (arithmetic)
findings.value: ≥14.0 A at 100 % efficiency; ≈15.0–16.3 A at techtest.org's measured 85.8–93.3 % efficiency
findings.source_title: techtest.org – Anker vs. UGREEN und Baseus: der Anker A2737 Nano Car Charger 167,5 W im Test
findings.note: 167.5 W ÷ 12 V = 13.96 A; ÷ 0.933 = 14.96 A; ÷ 0.858 = 16.27 A. techtest measured the A2737 holding ~90 W on a Framework 16 for 6:38 min then switching off and cycling, versus UGREEN CD293 (~5 min at 100 W then ~40 W) and Baseus BSCC-ZX-CCL (~15 min then ~40 W). techtest lists C1 PDOs 5 V/9 V/15 V 3 A, 20 V 5 A and PPS 5–11 V up to 5 A on both USB-C ports; C2 at 27 W PD in their test.

findings.label: price and stock, Anker US
findings.source_title: Anker Nano Car Charger (167.5W, 3 Ports) – Anker US
findings.note: Page shows 100 W USB-C1 and 45 W USB-C2; the spec tab with input current did not render in the fetched content.

findings.label: ports, PPS, cable, stock
findings.value: USB-C 30 W PD 3.0 with PPS + USB-A 12 W; no cable in box; $24.99, out of stock, 'Coming Soon by Tue Nov 24 2026'
findings.source_title: Belkin BoostCharge Dual Car Charger 42W – Belkin US
findings.note: Belkin's compatibility list includes MacBook Air 13" M1/M2 and Nintendo Switch 2; Belkin's 21-min iPhone 0–50 % claim was measured with a USB-C to USB-C cable that is not included in the standalone SKU. Input voltage is not stated on the page.

findings.label: what rivals already state
findings.value: supergrail: 12–24 V input for Anker 535 and UGREEN 130 W, '5A e-marked cable' for >60 W, 10 A fuse as example only; soldermag: Anker 535 45+9+9 W split
findings.source_title: Best USB-C Car Chargers in 2026 | SuperGrail
findings.note: Also read https://www.soldermag.com/posts/best-usb-c-car-chargers-2026 (2026-11-08), which says it is research-based without full bench testing. Neither page gives any charger's rated input amps or a vehicle socket rating.
